tools.name: get_tool_detail
tools.description: Get the full AgentIndex record for one tool when you already have its id (from search_tools, get_trending or an AgentIndex URL such as agentindex.app/en/tool/<id>/). Returns name, description, long intro, summary, features, use cases, pros and cons, when to choose or skip it, compatibility, install

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List every category in the AgentIndex directory with the number of tools in it, largest first. Call this before using the category filter of search_tools to get valid names, or to give the user an overview of the directory. Returns an array of {category, count}. Takes no arguments.

tools.description: Get the highest-ranked tools across the whole AgentIndex directory, for questions like "what are the best/most popular open-source AI tools right now". findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_categories" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List every category in the AgentIndex directory with the number of tools in it, largest first. Call this before using the category filter of search_tools to get…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_tool_detail, submit_tool · Private data: get_tool_detail, submit_tool · Public sink: submit_tool.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_tool_detail, submit_tool · Private data: get_tool_detail, submit_tool · Public sink: submit_tool

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
